Operations / Reliability and oversight

Data pipeline terminal failure rate

The percentage of terminal data pipeline run attempts ending in failure among attempts that ended in success or failure. Retried attempts count separately; canceled, queued, and running attempts are reported outside this denominator.

Explore in the metric hierarchy ↗Open calculators →
Level 4Inspect the detail

The percentage of terminal data pipeline run attempts ending in failure among attempts that ended in success or failure. Retried attempts count separately; canceled, queued, and running attempts are reported outside this denominator.

%

How we use it

We inspect recurring technical failures, retry behavior, and operational recovery while checking whether successful jobs produce valid business data.

Transparent calculationFailed terminal run attempts / (succeeded terminal run attempts + failed terminal run attempts) in the same window * 100
failed terminal attempts25
succeeded terminal attempts475

25 / (475 + 25) * 100 = 5% terminal-attempt failure rate.

Illustrative calculation. Not a client result or a universal benchmark.

Break the result down

  • Pipeline and activity
  • Failure reason and dependency
  • Attempt number and schedule

Questions we investigate

  • Which dependencies cause repeated failures?
  • Do retries recover jobs or repeat the same issue?
  • Are successful runs passing business validation?

Actions the evidence supports

  • Fix recurring dependency and configuration errors.
  • Set client-agreed retry and alert policies.
  • Pair technical monitoring with output validation.

Reporting contract

Ownership & cadence

Data engineering lead
Daily for reliability; immediate review of critical failures.

Required data

  • Unique run-attempt IDs and terminal statuses
  • Run timestamps, retry links, and failure codes
  • Business-output validation and recovery records

Read the measure with context

No succeeded-or-failed terminal attempts makes the rate undefined. Technical success does not prove data correctness. Attempt failure differs from eventual logical-job recovery; run duration, cancellation, and business validation need separate views.
